key_insight: CardioMeta is a calibrated multi-task model that jointly predicts diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease while emphasizing leakage reduction and reliability across different healthcare data sources.
clinical_relevance: It may support more trustworthy cardiometabolic risk prediction by producing better-calibrated probabilities, though performance drops under dataset shift and should not be assumed to generalize automatically.
method: Shared cardiometabolic encoder with disease-specific gated prediction heads
Post-hoc probability calibration to improve reliability
Primary analysis removed disease-defining variables; full feature set used only as sensitivity analysis
evidence_signal: Using NHANES for development and temporal validation plus MIMIC-IV for external EHR evaluation, the leakage-reduced setting achieved macro-AUROC 0.839, macro-AUPRC 0.536, macro-F1 0.614, and ECE 0.024.
watch_item: External performance degraded substantially in MIMIC-IV, so real-world deployment would require local validation, recalibration, and careful checking for label leakage and subgroup reliability.
paper_title: CardioMeta: Calibrated Multi-Task Prediction of Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cardiovascular Disease Across Population and EHR Data
